Tan Shih-ping (戴持平) alias Tan Pei-huei (戴璧輝) is the Chief Secretary of the Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhui General Revenue Bureau. He was arrested some time ago by the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters on suspicion of being connected with the attempt on the life of Chao Chih-chun (邵式軍), Commissioner of the Bureau, but has now been released on security furnished by the Commissioner. He has been reinstated as Chief Secretary of the Bureau.

FILE
Tan, who is an opium smoker, was formerly very poor. Since his appointment as Chief Secretary of the General Revenue Bureau, he has made a fortune of over $300,000. Many of his followers have joined the Bureau due to his introduction.

On a charge of misappropriation, Tan was at one time transferred to Anhui but thanks to the assistance rendered by Chao Chih-chun, the Commissioner, his conspirator in the misappropriation of funds, Tan managed to remain at his former post. Tan was arrested by the Japanese because the assailants who made the unsuccessful attempt on the life of Chao Chih-chun had been engaged on his recommendation. It is said that during his detention, he sustained many bodily injuries.

NOV 1 7 1938

PATRIOTIC CORPS
MEMBER RECEIVES
SUSPENDED TERM

Pleading guilty of attempted extortion, Zung Yoong-zai, the 16-year-old Fukienese who wrote threatening letters to Zau Sheh-chun, director of the puppet "Consolidated Tax Bureau of Chekiang, Kiangsu and Anhwei," received a suspended sentence of three months' imprisonment yesterday. The suspension will last for two years.

The leniency granted to him by the judge of the First Special District Court was believed due to the fact that in writing the threatening note, the youth's intention was merely to borrow money and not to intimidate the director. The accused was defended by Mr. C. Y. Loh.

It was also revealed by Mr. Loh yesterday that prior to his appointment to the present "enviable" post, the "director" once borrowed $100 from the youth's mother, who was then serving as amah in his house, through another amah.

Debt Settled

This debt was settled shortly after he became the "director" of the "Consolidated Tax Bureau," it was learned yesterday.

Altogether, the youth wrote three threatening letters, plus a fourth, polite one.

In the first letter, he demanded $100 from the "director"; in the second, $1,000; in the third, $2,000. None of them was replied to.

Feeling desperate, he wrote the fourth one on November 3, in which he declared that the sum of $2,000 had better be delivered, or else the blood of the "Hot-Blooded Youth Corps," of which the young Fukienese was member, would be aroused.

Zung was arrested by Detective Sub-Inspector F. O. Guess on November 6. At the court yesterday, he pleaded guilty, stating that he was in need of money to pursue his studies in a local middle school.

Zau Sheh-chun, the complainant, received the scare of his life last month when terrorists attempted to assassinate him on Nanking Road, while he was riding in his limousine. His bullet-proof car saved his life.

爱国团成员
获缓刑判决

福建籍16岁青年曾永载（Zung Yoong-zai，音译）因向伪“浙江、江苏及安徽统税局”局长邵式军（Zau Sheh-chun，音译）寄送恐吓信，承认企图勒索罪名成立，昨日被判处三个月监禁，缓刑执行。缓刑期为两年。

第一特区法院法官对其从轻发落，据信是因为该青年在写恐吓信时，意图仅是借钱，而非恐吓局长。被告由罗律师（Mr. C. Y. Loh）辩护。

罗律师昨日还透露，在该“局长”担任这一令人羡慕的职位之前，曾通过另一名女佣，向当时在他家做女佣的该青年母亲借款100元。

债务已清偿

据悉，这笔债务在他成为“统税局”“局长”后不久即已还清。

该青年总共写了三封恐吓信，外加一封措辞礼貌的信。

在第一封信中，他向“局长”索要100元；第二封信索要1,000元；第三封信索要2,000元。均未得到回复。

感到绝望之余，他于11月3日写了第四封信，声称最好交付2,000元，否则将激起这位福建青年所属的“热血青年团”的热血。

曾永载于11月6日被副督察 F. O. Guess 逮捕。在昨日的法庭上，他认罪，称需要钱在当地一所中学读书。

投诉人邵式军上月在南京路乘坐豪华轿车时遭遇恐怖分子刺杀未遂，吓得不轻。他的防弹车救了他一命。

NOV 9 1938

Puppet Tax Official Gets
Threatening Letter Series

Zau Si-chun, director of the Consolidated Tax Bureau for Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei Provinces of the "Reformed Government," recently saved from assassination by the bullet-proof windows of his automobile, is now the target of a mob of threatening letter writers, according to information in the hands of Shanghai Municipal Police.

The puppet official it is stated, started receiving threatening letters 10 days ago and, afraid that another attempt on his life might be made, has sought police investigation of the case.

One of three letters received to date demanded payment of $1,000 in cash. Unless payment were made, drastic action against the person of Zau was threatened.

Still another letter warned Zau that another attempt on his life would be made in the near future.

The third letter demanded a loan of $2,000. The latter missive, however, was not of a threatening nature and merely pointed out that the loan would be appreciated.

An amah in the employ of the Zau family has been detained for questioning by the police but no direct charges have been brought against her.

The attempt on Zau's life was made on October 10, when he was on his way to the Central Police Station to report an alleged misappropriation of tax funds.

He was riding in his car at the time and as the machine turned on Honan Road from Nanking Road, would-be assassins stepped into the picture and opened fire. The car was struck several times but the fact that it was armor plated and the windows were bullet proof saved Zau and four companions from being seriously wounded and perhaps killed.

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 29 1938

All Efforts Of Police To
Identify Terrorists Fail

No Arrests Made As Yet
In Connection With
Three Attacks

Despite evidence indicating that a newly-organized pro-Chinese terrorist band is still in this city, no progress is reported in police attempts to identify members of the organization.

Since the daring attempted assassination of Tsau Sheh-kung, general director of the Nippon-sponsored "Consolidated Tax Bureau," on October 17, when the puppet's heavily-armored car frustrated an audacious plot on his life, terrorists have been lying low.

Police are disinclined to connect Thursday's bombing of the Tung Sung Kong Shipping and Transportation Company on Kiangse Road with this particular group of terrorists, and believe that it was the work of a smaller and separate organization.

**Police Active**

This does not mean, however, that the police in both foreign-administered areas are idly awaiting another outburst of terrorism before they take action. Police agents in both the Settlement and Concession are constantly on the look-out for clues which might lead them to the arrest of at least one member of the terrorist band.

Since Monday, October 17, when Ya Ta-hsiung, counsellor to the puppet regime's "Ministry of Industries" was hacked to death at his New Asia Hotel headquarters, police have been expecting a fresh, intensified wave of terrorism. That same afternoon terrorists made the attempt on Tsau Sheh-kung's life at the corner of Nanking and Honan Roads, but have been inactive ever since.

**Fear Fresh Outburst**

Some quarters believe that the band has left Shanghai to return at a time when police vigilance will be more lax, but others fear that the gang is very much present in this city, and is only awaiting a favorable opportunity to strike.

In the past, it is pointed out, the lightning thrusts of pro-Chinese terrorists invariably revealed careful planning and careful adherence to the details of such clever plots. It is possible, THE CHINA PRESS learned, that the present calm is only an ominous quiet before a fresh outburst.

**No Arrests Made**

There have been no arrests made so far in either the axe murder at the New Asia Hotel or the attempt on Tsau Sheh-kung. As far as the New Asia Hotel murder is concerned, the matter is practically out of the hands of the Shanghai Municipal Police, for the Japanese are distinctly loathe to allow any sort of investigations to be carried on in the former headquarters of the puppet regime.

The French Police are also still searching for the assassins of Mr. Tang Shao-yi, 78-year-old statesman and former prime minister of China, who was hacked to death in his home at 18 Route Ferguson on September 30. The men who perpetrated the crime entered the well-guarded residence under pretext of bearing gifts for the impending wedding of their victim's daughter.

Recently the police offered a $15,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of two Cantonese, Peter Tse and Joseph Wang, who are believed to have been connected with the assassins.

實施任何逮捕

儘管有證據表明一個新組建的親華恐怖團伙仍在本市活動，但據報警方在識別該組織成員方面沒有取得進展。

自10月17日大膽企圖刺殺日本扶植的「統稅局」總辦曹世恭（Tsau Sheh-kung，音譯）以來，當時憑藉其重裝甲汽車挫敗了一項大膽的暗殺陰謀，恐怖分子一直潛伏不出。

警方不願將週四發生在江西路通勝公輪船運輸公司的爆炸案與這夥特定的恐怖分子聯繫起來，並認為那是另一個較小且獨立的組織所為。

**警方行動積極**

然而，這並不意味著兩個外僑管理區域的警方在採取行動之前，會消極等待下一次恐怖主義爆發。租界和法租界的警方特工不斷尋找線索，以期至少逮捕該恐怖團伙的一名成員。

自10月17日星期一，傀儡政權「實業部」顧問亞大雄（Ya Ta-hsiung，音譯）在其新亞酒店總部被斧頭砍死以來，警方一直預期會出現新一輪更激烈的恐怖主義浪潮。同日下午，恐怖分子在南京路與河南路路口企圖刺殺曹世恭，但此後一直沒有活動。

**擔心再次爆發**

某些方面認為，該團伙已離開上海，將在警方警戒較為鬆懈時返回，但其他人則擔心該幫派仍大量滯留本市，只是在等待有利的下手機會。

指出的是，過去親華恐怖分子的閃電式襲擊 invariably 顯示出周密的計劃以及對這些巧妙陰謀細節的嚴格遵循。據《字林西報》了解，目前的平靜可能只是新一輪爆發前不祥的寂靜。

**未實施逮捕**

截至目前，無論是新亞酒店的斧頭謀殺案還是針對曹世恭的未遂襲擊，均未實施逮捕。就新亞酒店謀殺案而言，此事實際上已不在上海公共租界工部局警务处的掌控之中，因為日本人明確不願允許在前傀儡政權總部進行任何形式的調查。

法國警察也在繼續搜尋刺殺78歲政治家、中國前總理唐紹儀先生的兇手，唐於9月30日在其費倫路18號家中被斧頭砍死。作案者以贈送受害者女兒即將舉行的婚禮禮物為藉口，進入了戒備森嚴的住宅。

最近，警方懸賞15,000美元，徵集能導致逮捕兩名廣東人彼得·謝（Peter Tse）和約瑟夫·王（Joseph Wang）的信息，據信他們與刺客有關聯。

October 27, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao:

THE DISAPPEARANCE OF A TAX BUREAU OFFICIAL

The disappearance of Tai Pih-hui (戴陸輝), Chief Secretary to the Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhwei Consolidated Tax Bureau, is causing much anxiety among the puppet officials in this locality. The officials of the Bureau are at a loss to understand what has happened to the Chief Secretary, with the exception, of course, of Zau Shih-chun (印式軍), the Chief, who is fully aware of the facts.

Information from reliable quarters reveals that after securing the post of Chief Secretary, Tai Pih-hui conspired with Zau Shih-chun and other members of the staff of the Bureau to carry out corrupt practices. Thus, in less than one year a considerable fortune has been amassed by both Tai Pih-hui and Zau Shih-chun. The Japanese authorities heard something about this but they could not secure the necessary evidence. Three months ago, certain persons made a complaint direct to Tokyo whereupon Doihara was despatched here to make an investigation. Through the influence of Kusumoto and Takahashi, the matter was shelved. On the birthday anniversary of the Japanese Emperor, Zau Shih-chun remitted $1,000,000 to Japan in order to please the authorities. Thus, the position of Zau Shih-chun has become stronger.

The Japanese authorities believe that the attempt on the life of Zau Shih-chun on Nanking Road was due to dissension amongst the puppet officials, because it is difficult for outsiders to learn Zau's movements. Investigation has revealed that the person arrested on the morning of October 21 for making an attempt on Zau's life is a former employee of the Consolidated Tax Bureau who had been recommended by Tai Pih-hui. The arrested person stated that the plot was arranged by Tai Pih-hui, because the latter was indignant over Zau's action in monopolising control over the several million dollars which had been collected through plans made by Tai Pih-hui.

Upon receipt of this information, the Japanese military authorities at noon October 22 detailed two Japanese detectives to the Consolidated Tax Bureau, who carried off Tai Pih-hui to the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters for detention.

**稅務局官員失蹤**

江蘇浙江安徽統稅局秘書長戴陸輝（Tai Pih-hui，戴陸輝）的失蹤，引起了本地傀儡官員們的極大焦慮。除了完全知曉內情的局長鄒式軍（Zau Shih-chun，印式軍）外，該局官員們對秘書長的遭遇感到困惑不解。

來自可靠渠道的消息顯示，戴陸輝在獲得秘書長職位後，與鄒式軍及該局其他職員勾結，進行貪污腐敗活動。因此，在不到一年的時間裡，戴陸輝和鄒式軍都積攢了巨額財富。日本當局對此有所耳聞，但未能獲取必要證據。三個月前，某些人士直接向東京投訴，隨後土肥原（Doihara）被派往此地進行調查。通過楠本（Kusumoto）和高橋（Takahashi）的影響，此事被擱置。在日本天皇誕辰紀念日，鄒式軍向日本匯款100萬美元以討好當局。因此，鄒式軍的地位變得更加穩固。

日本當局認為，南京路針對鄒式軍的未遂襲擊是由於傀儡官員之間的內訌所致，因為外人很難獲悉鄒的行蹤。調查顯示，10月21日上午因企圖襲擊鄒而被捕的人，是一名前統稅局員工，由戴陸輝推薦。被捕者聲稱，該陰謀由戴陸輝策劃，因為後者對鄒獨佔控制通過戴陸輝的計劃籌集的數百萬美元資金感到憤怒。

收到此情報後，日本軍方當局於10月22日中午派遣兩名日本偵探前往統稅局，將戴陸輝帶往日本憲兵隊總部羈押。

Shun Pao :-

CHIEF SECRETARY TO CONSOLIDATED TAX BUREAU MISSING

Tai Pih-hui (戴際輝), Chief Secretary to the Consolidated Tax Bureau for Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei on Kiukiang Road, was reported missing on October 22.
Tai Pih-hui is also known as Tai Sz-ping (戴梓平), age 48, a native of Kweichow. For many years, he served with the Chinese military and political authorities and at one time he was secretary to the late Mr. Hu Han-min (胡漢民). On the outbreak of hostilities on August 13, 1937, he was in Shanghai and was a follower of Hsu Pao-ziang (許寶祥) a former Divisional Commander. On the recommendation of Hsu Pao-ziang, Zau Shih-chun (鄒式軍) became acquainted with Colonel Kusumoto after the fall of Shanghai, and later secured the post of Chief of the Consolidated Tax Bureau.
Colonel Kusumoto instructed Zau Shih-chun to draft a set of measures on the management of the Consolidated Tax Bureau. As Zau knew only how to smoke opium, he did nothing. At about this time Hsu Pao-ziang found Tai Pih-hui in a certain refugee camp and asked Tai to draft measures on behalf of Zau Shih-chun. The measures were prepared and Zau gave them to Colonel Kusumoto. As a result, Zau was appointed Chief of the Consolidated Tax Bureau and Tai became Chief Secretary.
Zau has since accumulated a fortune of several million dollars. Tai resides at No. 1, Mei Tsung (梅村), Connaught Road in the extra-Settlement roads area in the Western District and used to attend office at 9 a.m. every day. Realizing his danger, Zau Shih-chun does not attend office regularly, therefore, all the affairs of the Consolidated Tax Bureau were handled by Tai.
At 9 a.m. October 22, Tai visited the Consolidated Tax Bureau as usual and at 11 a.m. he was reported missing. The Police watchmen at the gate of the Bureau did not see Tai walk out. At 11 a.m. that day, certain persons saw Tai together with two Japanese in the lift going from the 3rd floor to the 2nd floor.
Our reporter yesterday met a certain junior employee of the Consolidated Tax Bureau and was informed that very strict precautions have been adopted in the Bureau. Anybody visiting the Bureau to pay tax must first produce a pass before being allowed admittance.
After the disappearance of Tai Pih-hui, Zau Shih-chun ordered all the employees of the Bureau to keep the matter absolutely secret. It was reported last night that Tai had been arrested by the Japanese because he was planning to embezzle the savings funds of the employees of the Bureau, amounting to some $200,000 and that Tai had been handed over to Zau Shih-chun for detention in Zau's house at No. 39 Nanyang Road. However, this information is not true.
Information secured from other sources shows that it is true that Tai has been arrested by the Japanese on suspicion that he is connected with the attempt on the life of Zau Shih-chun on Nanking Road the other day. It was also reported that when Tai took over his post, he sent a man named Tih Yih-tsing (狄一青) to Hongkong to conduct certain activities.

**統稅局秘書長失蹤**

據報，九江路江蘇浙江安徽統稅局秘書長戴際輝（Tai Pih-hui，戴際輝）於10月22日失蹤。
戴際輝又名戴梓平（Tai Sz-ping，戴梓平），48歲，貴州人。多年來，他在中國軍政當局任職，並曾擔任已故胡漢民（Hu Han-min，胡漢民）先生的秘書。1937年8月13日戰事爆發時，他在上海，是前師長許寶祥（Hsu Pao-ziang，許寶祥）的追随者。經許寶祥推薦，鄒式軍（Zau Shih-chun，鄒式軍）在上海淪陷後結識了楠本上校，隨後獲得了統稅局局長的職位。
楠本上校指示鄒式軍起草一套統稅局管理措施。由於鄒只懂吸食鴉片，他什麼也沒做。大約在此時，許寶祥在某個難民營找到了戴際輝，請戴代鄒式軍起草措施。措施擬定後，鄒將其交給了楠本上校。結果，鄒被任命為統稅局局長，戴成為秘書長。
此後，鄒積累了數百萬美元的財富。戴居住在西区越界築路區域康納特路梅村1號，過去每天上午9點上班。意識到危險的鄒式軍不經常去辦公室，因此，統稅局的所有事務均由戴處理。
10月22日上午9點，戴像往常一樣來到統稅局，上午11點時據報失蹤。局門口的警察崗哨沒有看到戴走出大門。當天上午11點，有人看到戴與兩名日本人一起乘坐電梯從三樓下到二樓。
我們的記者昨天會見了統稅局的一名初級職員，得知該局已採取非常嚴格的預防措施。任何前來繳稅的人必須先出示通行證方可進入。
戴際輝失蹤後，鄒式軍命令該局所有員工對此事絕對保密。昨晚有報道稱，戴因企圖侵吞該局員工儲蓄基金（約20萬美元）而被日本人逮捕，並已被移交給鄒式軍，羈押在鄒位於南陽路39號的寓所。然而，此消息不實。
從其他來源獲得的信息顯示，戴確實因涉嫌與日前南京路針對鄒式軍的未遂襲擊有關而被日本人逮捕。另有報道稱，戴上任時，曾派遣一名叫狄一青（Tih Yih-tsing，狄一青）的人前往香港進行某些活動。

正如报案人及其一名保镖在陈述中所述，似乎下午5点后不久，当他乘坐汽车离开办公室后院的院落时，有人告知他九江路与河南路路口有不少人徘徊，因此他指示司机沿九江路向东驶往江西路，而不是像通常那样向西行驶。到达江西路后，司机随即向北转弯，然后沿南京路向西行驶至枪击发生地点。鉴于此情况并研究了该地区的布局，具名人认为，企图暗杀者的原意是在河南路与九江路路口实施暗杀，因为那里比南京路更合适；然而，当他们看到汽车在九江路上向东行驶，随后在江西路上向北行驶时，他们立即改变了计划，穿过从九江路通向南京路、并从巧克力店旁出来的小巷，正好赶上报案人的汽车沿南京路向西驶来，

and opened fire, as was seen by Mr. Gordon Gordon from
his studio window, which overlooks this alleyway and
Nanking Road facing West. Having completed their job,
both these men seperated one running into the Liao Kah
Fook (老介福) silk store (corroborated by the finding
of the pistol and ammunition therein), whilst the other
is alleged to have run East towards Kiangse Road. This
latter move is corroborated by Mr. Gordon Gordon, how-
ever in view of the fact that this gentleman's office
is located on the 2nd. floor of the building in question
and looks West, his word cannot altogether be accepted
and it is the opinion of the undersigned that this
second man did not run towards Kiangse Road, but doubled
back down this alleyway onto Kuikiang Road, and in this
manner made good his escape. In view of this latter
theory detectives are now making enquiries in the
vicinity of this alleyway, with a view to, if possible,
locating further witnesses.

In reference to the undermentioned six persons
arrested by D.S. J.N. Binkson in connection with the
embezzlement of $40,000.00 from the Consolidated Tax
Bureau (See F.I.R.2507/38 Central) all have been subject
to lengthy interrogation, resulting in each making a
written statement, copies of which are attached, however

关于由副督察J.N. Binkson因联合税务局贪污40,000.00美元一案逮捕的下列六人（参见中央捕房F.I.R.2507/38号报告），所有人都接受了长时间的审讯，每人均作了书面陈述，副本附后，然而

关于在犯罪现场缴获的.32口径毛瑟自动手枪一支（编号527052），连同弹匣一个及.32口径自动子弹6发，该枪支已于1938年10月17日晚送交枪械鉴定科，结果发现该枪支无既往记录，在现场捡到的两个弹壳以及从报案人车内取出的八颗子弹也无既往记录。经鉴定，其中一个弹壳和从报案人车内取出的七颗子弹系由缴获的手枪射出，而剩下的一个弹壳和子弹则被发现是由另一支枪射出，因此使用的武器总数为两支（参见枪械鉴定科第4224/38号报告）。

Regarding the pistol seized, it is worthy of
note that the serial number of same comes within the
consignment purchase from the Mauser Company on behalf
of the Nationalist Government by the Chinese Ambassador
to Germany in the latter part of 1937. Of this consign-
ment, twelve similiar pistols have already been seized
by the S.M.Police and French Police in connection with
other political assassinations.

As result of a finger print examination of the
seized gun by D.S.I. J. Dickson i/c Finger Print Bureau
no finger prints were secured (See C.2 Report No.6710/38).

On the afternoon of 18/10/38 Mr. Muir of the
Shanghai Tramways communicated to the undersigned, by

this shooting affray a window in Trailer No.234 of a
No.6 Route Tramcar had been shattered by a bullet,
which had apparently gone straight through same. As
far as Mr. Muir could state no persons had been injured
and the bullet could not be found.

Endeavours are being continued regarding the
possibility of inside collusion in connection with
this offence.

关于此案是否存在内部勾结的可能性，调查工作仍在继续。

Chu Ping Sing( 朱丙莘 ).
Szechuen.                                      D.S. Fowler.
C.B.H.Q.(C.S)             17-10-38             D.S.I. Chu Shou Ling.

My name is Chu Ping Sing( 朱丙莘 ), age 23, native of
Szechuen , S/unemployed and at present residing at Lane 668
House 129 Yu Yuen Road, the home of my sister Chu Chung Wun
( 朱中文 ), who is married to one Shui Ts Wei( 水次惠 )an
employee in the Salt Gabelle in Chungking.

I was born in Peking on the 26th day of the 7 month 1911.
I attended Schools in Peking until the age of 17 when I
studied for two years at the Nankai University, Tientsin. I
then studied at the Catholic University, Peking, for one year and
finally at the China University, Peking for three years. I
was then 22 years old on graduating.

I was unable to secure work for several months but finally
succeeded in doing so as a teacher at the Lee Ming Middle
School( 黎明中学 ), Peking, for 6 months. I was again unemployed
for several months.

In about November 1935 I went to Hangchow where I secured a
position as assistant accountant with the Chekiang Provincial
Government, construction department.

I October 1937, I was transferred to the Highway
Engineering Department and stayed there until the beginning of
March 1938 when the department was disbanded owing to hostilities.

My father and mother having died, I came to Shanghai and live
lived with my sister in Yu Yuen Road. She provides me with
pocket-money as I have been unable to find work in Shanghai.

At about 3.30 p.m. October 17th, 1938 I left my sister's
home and proceeded by No. 1 bus to Yates Road and from there walk-
ed to the Tian Chang ( 天昌 )Photo Shop, Bubbling Well Road,
pages.zh:
朱丙莘（Chu Ping Sing）。
四川籍。                                      副督察 Fowler。
中央捕房总部(刑事股)             1938年10月17日             副督察长 朱守灵。

我叫朱丙莘（Chu Ping Sing），23岁，四川籍，目前无业，现居住在愚园路668弄129号我姐姐朱中文（Chu Chung Wun）家中，她嫁给了水次惠（Shui Ts Wei），后者是重庆盐务稽核所的职员。

我于1911年7月26日出生于北京。我在北京上学直到17岁，随后在天津南开大学学习了两年。之后我在北京辅仁大学（Catholic University）学习了一年，最后在北京中国大学学习了三年。毕业时我22岁。

我有几个月没能找到工作，但最终在北京黎明中学（Lee Ming Middle School）找到了一份教师的工作，干了6个月。之后我又失业了几个月。

大约在1935年11月，我去了杭州，在浙江省政府建设厅找到了一份助理会计的职位。

1937年10月，我被调往公路工程处，一直工作到1938年3月初，因战事该部门解散。

父母去世后，我来到上海，与姐姐住在愚园路。由于我在上海找不到工作，她给我提供零用钱。

1938年10月17日下午3点30分左右，我离开姐姐家，乘1路公交车前往亚尔培路（Yates Road），然后从那里步行至静安寺路的天昌（Tian Chang）照相馆，

pages.en:
- 2 -

where I was to meet a friend named Sze Chi Fah(施啓藩)who had
telephoned me at my sister's home. I met Sze and learned from
him that the photos he was wanting were at Young's Photo Shop,
on Nanking Road near Honan Road.

We proceeded by a No. 1 M/bus to Nanking--Yu Ya Ching Roads
where my friend went into the Sun Company regarding a purchase
and on coming out we again took a No. 1 M/bus to Nanking--Honan
Roads where we alighted and went to Young's Photo Shop. On the
business being completed we came out and intended catching a
No. 1 bus to return to Yu Yuen Road. The buses however were
crowded at that time(about 5.15 p.m.)and we decided to take a
tramcar and had just crossed Honan Road on the south side of
Nanking Road when we heard the sound of shots a few yards away,
we both laid flat on the pavement and on the firing ceasing ran
into a silk store where, a few minutes later a party of Police
arrived and from a large number of persons in the shop, I and my
friend were brought to Central Station.

I did not see who fired the shots or at what or whom they
were firing.

I have never received any political training neither
having I had any military training.

The foregoing is a true statement.

Signed.

我要去见一位名叫施啓藩（Sze Chi Fah）的朋友，他此前曾在我姐姐家给我打过电话。我见到了施，并从他那里得知，他想要的照片在位于南京路近河南路的杨氏照相馆（Young's Photo Shop）。

我们乘坐1路公共汽车前往南京路与亚尔培路（Yu Ya Ching Roads，即今延安东路）路口，我的朋友进入先施公司（Sun Company）购物，出来后我们再次乘坐1路公共汽车前往南京路与河南路路口，下车后前往杨氏照相馆。办完事后我们出来，打算乘坐1路公共汽车返回愚园路。然而当时（约下午5点15分）公共汽车非常拥挤，我们决定改乘电车。当我们刚穿过南京路南侧的河南路时，听到几码外传来枪声，我们两人都趴在人行道上，枪声停止后，我们跑进一家丝绸店。几分钟后，一队警察赶到，将我和我的朋友从店内的众多人员中带出，送往中央捕房。

我没有看到是谁开的枪，也没有看到他们向什么或向谁开枪。

我从未接受过任何政治训练，也未接受过任何军事训练。

以上陈述属实。

签名。

Koo Ts Tsoong.
Nanzing.                                      D.S.I. Crighton.
C.B.H.Q.(C.8)          19-10-38.              D.S.I. Wong.

My name is Koo Ts Tsoong(顾治中), age 24, native of
Nanzing, single clerk, employed at the Consolidated Tax Bureau
230 Kiukiang Road, and residing at 63 Tsau Foong Bi Su(北丰别墅)
Brenan Road.
    I was born at Nanzing, 17-7-25, my parents then being the
owners of the Ju Yuen(聚源) Pawnshop in Hangchow, also my
father was a share-holder in the Huchow Power Company.
Between the ages of 7 and 14 years I studied under a private
tutor named Doo Pah Sung(屠伯崇) at my home in Nanzing. At
the age of 14 years I entered the Nanzing Middle School and
remained therein until I attained the age of 19 years when I
came to Shanghai and entered the Shanghai Young Men's High
School. Graduating from this school at the age of 21 years I
entered Kwong Hwa (光华) University, however owing to the
outbreak of hostilities in August 1937, I left Shanghai and
returned to my native place at Nanzing, where I remained for
two months, later returning to Shanghai in an attempt to assist
my uncle in transporting rice from Nanzing to Shanghai. At
this time I resided in the Central Hotel, however as this was
not convenient I later took a house in the Ziang Kong Li(祥康里)
off Myburgh Road. Being unable to carry out this transporta-
tions business, especially after Nanzing fell into the Japanese
Military, I stated looking for work and through a friend named
Chen Wei Ming(邱惠民) I was successful in obtaining the
position of clerk in the Consolidated Tax Bureau, first under
Zau Dau S(邱读是) and later under the present Chief cashier
Pau Liang Tsoo(潘良佐). Everything went well until March 1938
when my family came to Shanghai and I was forced to support
pages.zh:
顾治中。
南京。                                      副督察长 Crighton。
中央捕房总部 (C.8)          1938年10月19日。              副督察长 Wong。

我叫顾治中（Koo Ts Tsoong），24岁，南京人，未婚，职员，受雇于九江路230号的统税局，居住在勃伦安路（Brenan Road，即今圆明园路）63号北丰别墅（Tsau Foong Bi Su）。
    我于1925年7月17日出生于南京，当时我的父母是杭州聚源（Ju Yuen）当铺的所有者，此外我的父亲也是湖州电力公司（Huchow Power Company）的股东。
7岁至14岁期间，我在南京家中跟随一位名叫屠伯崇（Doo Pah Sung）的私人教师学习。14岁时，我进入南京中学就读，直至19岁来到上海，进入上海青年会中学（Shanghai Young Men's High School）。21岁从该校毕业后，我进入光华大学（Kwong Hwa University）就读，然而由于1937年8月战事爆发，我离开上海回到家乡南京，在那里停留了两个月，随后返回上海，试图帮助我的叔叔将大米从南京运往上海。当时我住在中央饭店（Central Hotel），但因不便，后来在迈尔西爱路（Myburgh Road，即今茂名南路）附近的祥康里（Ziang Kong Li）租了一处房屋。由于无法开展这项运输业务，特别是在南京沦陷于日军之后，我开始寻找工作，并通过一位名叫邱惠民（Chen Wei Ming，注：原文拼音与中文名不符，此处依中文名译）的朋友，成功获得了统税局职员的职位，起初在邱读是（Zau Dau S，音译）手下工作，后来在现任首席出纳潘良佐（Pau Liang Tsoo）手下工作。一切顺利，直到1938年3月，我的家人来到上海，我被迫供养

them. My father having lost everything in the war. At this time
I was drawing $60.00 per month and finding I could not keeping
my family and myself on this amount, I asked for an increase,
which resulted in me getting $110.00 in May. Since that I have
been drawing this latter amount monthly, however with the
increase in rents, food etc. I was little the better for this
increase and gradually I found myself getting deeply into debt,
in fact so bad did it get that I even borrowed a pair of gold
bangles from a lady friend and sold them to a gold shop for
$180.00. At the end of last month I could not meet my usual month-
ly expenses, hence I using my uncle's old cheque book wrote
out a post dated cheque for $150.00 which was accepted by one of
my friends named Chu Bei Ju(邱倍球)who gave me cash for same.
Even with this money however I could not liquidate my debts
sheer desperation, I mentioned to my boss Pau Liang Tsoo(潘良佐)
that as I was in such a state I attended committing suicide.
He hearing me say this said, "Why do that" and in a sort
of joking way added, "Why don't you embezzle money from the
office and run away. Although I gave this remark no thought at
that time, it gradually began to play in my mind, and eventually
about one week ago I decided that I would try and embezzle some
money from my office in order to cover my debts which by this
time had amounted to about $100.00. Here I must add that I was
also worried about the cheque I had taken from my uncle as it was
due for presentation at the Bank on the 17-10-38 and I knew that
there was no money to meet it.
On the night of 16-10-38 whilst I was in the Sun Ballroom
pages.zh:

他们。我的父亲在战争中失去了一切。当时我月薪60美元，发现这笔钱不足以维持我和家人的生活，我便要求加薪，结果在5月份涨到了110美元。此后我一直领取这一数额的月薪，然而随着房租、食品等价格的上涨，这次加薪对我帮助不大，渐渐地我发现自己债台高筑，情况糟糕到我甚至从一位女性朋友那里借了一对金手镯，并以180美元的价格卖给了一家金店。上个月底，我无法支付每月的日常开销，因此我使用我叔叔的旧支票簿开出了一张金额为150美元的远期支票，这张支票被我的一个名叫邱倍球（Chu Bei Ju，音译）的朋友接受，他为此付给了我现金。然而即使有了这笔钱，我也无法清偿债务，在极度绝望中，我向老板潘良佐提及，鉴于我处于这种境地，我曾考虑自杀。他听我这么说，问道：“何必那样做”，并半开玩笑地补充说：“你为什么不挪用公款潜逃呢。”虽然当时我并未将此话放在心上，但它逐渐在我脑海中盘旋，最终大约在一周前，我决定尝试从办公室挪用一些钱以偿还债务，此时债务总额已达约100美元。在此我必须补充说明，我也为我从我叔叔那里拿来的支票感到担忧，因为该支票将于1938年10月17日在银行提示付款，而我知道账户中没有资金支付。
1938年10月16日晚，当我在大都会舞厅（Sun Ballroom）时

pages.en:

along with Yau Yau Nyi(姚予儀)and his ex-wife Yau Zung So
(姚沈氏)I mentioned to them that I was in a terrible position
as at least I must have seven hundred dollars by the following
day otherwise I would get into serious trouble both stated they
could not assist me, however I hinted to them that I had formed
a plan whereby I could get the money. At about 10 a.m. 17-10-30
I went to the office as usual and at this time Pau Liang Tsoo
(潘良佐)and Yau Yay Nyi(姚予儀)were present. At about 11 a.m
deciding to carry out my plan hence I went to the "Collecting
Department" and informed one named Zee Peng Zai(徐炳遂)that our
department, i.e. "Cashier," wanted money in a hurry. Zee(徐)
replied that he only had about $200.00 in hand, and I informed
him that this was not sufficient and returned to my own department
where I waited until about 11.20 a.m. when I saw the boss Pau
Liang Tsoo(潘良佐)going out. Seeing this I took the
opportunity to slip downstairs to the "Collecting Department"
again and this time I told Zee (徐)that we must have money
for the cashier department and that it was very urgent. Hearing
this Zee(徐)produced $500.00 in notes but I told him that
this was not sufficient and that we needed a large amount. Zee
then produced several cheques amongst which I noticed a "Pay to
bearer" cash cheque for $40,000.00. As this was the only cash
cheque he had I decided to take it, after which I left the office
and went to the National Commercial Bank where I cashed the said
cheque in the following manner:-$6,000.00 in cash, $30,000.00
Native Bank Order(crossed) $4,000.00 Native Bank Order(crossed).
My idea in getting the crossed Native Bank Orders was that it was
my intention to return same to the Bureau. Leaving the Bank
pages.zh:
- 3 -
与姚予儀（Yau Yau Nyi）及其前妻姚沈氏（Yau Zung So）在一起，我向他们提及我的处境极其糟糕，因为第二天之前我至少需要七百美元，否则我会陷入严重的麻烦。两人都表示无法协助我，但我向他们暗示我已经制定了一个搞到钱的计划。1938年10月17日上午10点左右，我像往常一样去办公室，当时潘良佐和姚予儀在场。上午11点左右，我决定执行我的计划，于是我去“收款部”，告诉一个叫徐炳遂（Zee Peng Zai，音译）的人，我们要部门，即“出纳部”，急需资金。徐回答说手头只有约200美元，我告诉他这不够，便回到自己的部门，等到上午11点20分左右，我看到老板潘良佐外出。见此情景，我趁机溜下楼再次来到“收款部”，这次我告诉徐，出纳部必须拿到钱，而且非常紧急。听到这话，徐拿出了500美元现钞，但我告诉他这还不够，我们需要一大笔钱。随后徐拿出几张支票，其中我注意到一张金额为40,000美元的“付持票人”现金支票。由于这是他唯一的现金支票，我决定拿走它，之后我离开办公室前往国家商业银行（National Commercial Bank），通过以下方式兑现了上述支票：6,000美元现金，30,000美元划线庄票（Native Bank Order），4,000美元划线庄票。我获取划线庄票的想法是，我打算将其归还给局里。离开银行后

pages.en:
- 4 -

I next proceeded to the Central Savings Society where I met my
friend Yuen Ping Sheng(袁炳鑫). I called him outside and after
explaining what had happened asked him to keep $3,000.00 for me.
At first he refused but later he agreed and I handed this amount
to him in Room 410 of the Weida Hotel which I had engaged that
day. I then telephoned home and requested my young brother to
come there. At about 2 p.m. that afternoon my brother came to
the Weida Hotel and to him I handed the two native Bank orders
along with a letter and requested him to send them to Pau Liang
Tsoo(潘良佐). I also gave him $800.00 and asked him to
square up all my debts as it was my intention to leave for Hong-
kong as soon as possible. After half an hour my brother left
and I then telephone to Yau Yeu Nyi's ex-wife and requested her
to come to the Weida Hotel. She arrived some time latter and
I gave her $200.00 which I owed her also I gave her another
$40.00 and asked her to go out and buy me some clothing including
a hat. She agreed to do so after hearing the story and left the
Hotel promising to return later. I then left the hotel and
proceeded to an exchange shop where I bought $150.00 Hongkong
Currency and then proceeded to various shipping Companies with a
view to arranging a ship to Hongkong. Unfortunately I could not
get a boat, and I returned to the Hotel, where on arrival I
phoned to Yuen Ping Sheng(袁炳鑫) requesting him to call on me.
He arrived at the Hotel at about 6 p.m. and I asked him to keep
a further $1,729.00 including the $150.00 Hongkong currency for
me as I explained it was dangerous for me to keep same in the
hotel, especially when I could not yet get a boat for Hongkong.
pages.zh:
- 4 -

我接着前往中央储蓄会（Central Savings Society），在那里遇到了我的朋友袁炳鑫（Yuen Ping Sheng）。我把他叫到外面，解释了发生的事情后，请他替我保管3,000美元。起初他拒绝了，但后来同意了，我在当天预订的伟达酒店（Weida Hotel）410房间将这笔钱交给了他。随后我打电话回家，让我的弟弟来那里。当天下午2点左右，我弟弟来到伟达酒店，我将两张庄票连同一封信交给他，请他将它们送给潘良佐。我还给了他800美元，让他还清我所有的债务，因为我打算尽快前往香港。半小时后我弟弟离开，随后我打电话给姚予儀的前妻，请她来伟达酒店。她稍后到达，我给了她欠她的200美元，另外又给了她40美元，让她出去帮我买些衣物，包括一顶帽子。听完原委后她答应照办，离开酒店并承诺稍后回来。随后我离开酒店，前往一家兑换店购买了150港元，然后前往各家轮船公司，试图安排前往香港的船只。不幸的是，我没能订到船位，于是返回酒店，到达后我打电话给袁炳鑫，请他来见我。他大约在下午6点到达酒店，我请他再替我保管1,729美元，其中包括150港元，因为我解释说，把这笔钱留在酒店很危险，尤其是当我还未能弄到去香港的船票时。

pages.en:
- 5 -

He took this money and left the hotel about 7.30 p.m.
I then ordered a M/car and was on my way to the Park Hotel for
the purpose of engaging a room there, but decided that it was not
safe and returned to the Weida Hotel. Later that night I was
arrested by detectives of the S.M.Police.

Ques. Have you ever been in any similar trouble before?
Ans. No, I have never.
Ques. Whilst a school, what course did you study?
Ans. I studied "Accountancy."
Ques. Have you ever studied Politics?
Ans. No.
Ques. Have you at any time ever been a member of any political
association.
Ans. No, I have never.
Ques. After office hours do you ever meet any of your old school mates
or other persons not connected with the Tax Bureau.
Ans. No, since I joined the Bureau I have lost most of my friends,
and the only person I really associate with after work is Yau Y
You Hyi(姚予儀)and Yen Ping Sheng(袁炳鑫 ).
Ques. Prior to the Commission of the Embezzlement did you discuss
the crime with anyone, either in your office or outside?
Ans. I discussed it with no one, as I was afraid that I might be
found out.
Ques. Were you not approached by someone, who requested you to carry
out this Embezzlement for the purpose of having Chao Shih
Chuen(邵式軍 )attend his office?
Ans. I did this case solely on my own and no one made any such
pages.zh:
- 5 -

他收下这笔钱，大约在晚上7点30分离开酒店。
随后我叫了一辆机动出租车，正前往国际饭店（Park Hotel）打算在那里订个房间，但觉得那里不安全，便返回伟达酒店。当晚晚些时候，我被工部局警务处的侦探逮捕。

问：你以前是否遇到过类似的麻烦？
答：不，从来没有。
问：上学期间，你修习什么课程？
答：我修习“会计学”。
问：你是否学习过政治学？
答：没有。
问：你是否曾在任何时候加入过任何政治团体？
答：不，从来没有。
问：下班后，你是否会见任何老同学或与统税局无关的其他人？
答：不，自从加入局里以来，我失去了大多数朋友，下班后我真正交往的只有姚予儀（Yau Y You Hyi，音译）和袁炳鑫（Yen Ping Sheng，音译）。
问：在实施挪用公款之前，你是否在办公室内或外部与任何人讨论过此罪行？
答：我没有与任何人讨论，因为我担心会被发现。
问：是否有人接近你，要求你实施此次挪用公款，目的是为了让邵式軍（Chao Shih Chuen）来到他的办公室？
答：此案完全是我个人所为，没有人向我提出此类

pages.en:
- 6 -

request to me.

Ques. You mention that you were only in debt to the extent of $1000.00
yet you refused to accept the $3,000.00 cheque from Zee Ping Zai (
(徐炳泰) when he offered it to you and instead said your office
wanted a larger amount, why?

Ans. My reason for such, is that the $3,000.00 cheque was post dated
until the 20th October hence it was no use to me then, whilst all
other cheques with the exception of the $40,000.00 were crossed
and not "Pay to bearer," hence I took the $40,000.00 one as I
knew it would be easy to cash.

Ques. Was it not the case that you knew that it would have to be
a large amount before you could draw Mr. Chao Shih Chuen
(邵式軍) to his office.

Ans. Such is not the case and I never thought of such a thing, again I
repeat that this Embezzlement was done by my own initiative
and nobody's instigation.

Ques. Have you ever heard anyone in the Tax Bureau discussing Mr.
Chao Shih Chuen in an unfavourable manner, or has anyone every
sounded you regarding your feelings towards the Nationalist
Government.

Ans. I have never heard Mr. Chao discussed unfavourably nor had anyone
spoke to me of my political feelings.

Ques. Can you of your own knowledge give any explanations as to who
would be most likely to have given the information that Mr.
Chao would attend the office that afternoon.

Ans. I can give no information in this respect, but I know for a
fact that when Mr. Chao intends visiting his office only the
pages.zh:
- 6 -

要求。

问：你提到你的债务仅为1,000美元，然而当徐炳泰（Zee Ping Zai，音译）向你提供3,000美元的支票时你却拒绝接受，反而说你们办公室需要更大的金额，为什么？

答：我这样做的原因是，那张3,000美元的支票是远期支票，到期日为10月20日，因此当时对我无用，而除40,000美元支票外的其他所有支票都是划线支票，并非“付持票人”，因此我拿了40,000美元的那张，因为我知道它容易兑现。

问：难道不是因为你认为必须是一笔巨款才能将邵式軍先生引到他的办公室吗？

答：事实并非如此，我从未想过这样的事，我再次重申，这次挪用公款是我主动发起的，并非受人唆使。

问：你是否听过统税局任何人以不利的方式讨论邵式軍先生，或者是否有人试探过你对国民政府的态度？

答：我从未听到有人不利地讨论邵先生，也从未有人与我谈论我的政治立场。

问：凭你所知，你能解释谁最有可能泄露邵先生那天下午会去办公室的消息吗？

答：在这方面我无法提供任何信息，但我确切知道，当邵先生打算视察其办公室时，只有

pages.en:
higher officials of the Bureau.have knowledge of this.
This is my true statement.

Signed.
pages.zh:
局里的高级官员知晓此事。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名。

pages.en:
Kee Kya Tseong ( 顾家声 ) alias Siau Poh
Nanzing D.S. Rhodes
H.Qrs 19.10.38 C.D.S. 273.

My name is Kee Kya Tseong (顾家声) alias Siau Poh (小
P宝) aged 20 years, native Nanzing, and at present residing at
No 63 Chang Feng Pih Su Brenan Road.

I was born at Nanzing, my father at that time being the
owner of a pawnshop at Hangchow. When I was eight years of age
I commenced school at the S Ngih a small school situated in
Nanzing, and remained thereat until I was twelve.

From the age of twelve until I was fourteen I studied at the
Nanzing Middle School and then transferred to the Tung Wee
Middle School also at Nanzing, where I remained until I was
sixteen years old. Leaving the latter school I and my elder
brother named Kee Ts Tseeng (顾恺中) came to Shanghai and
entered the Tsing Nan (青年) Middle School, (Young Men's
High School) situated at Avenue Joffre F.C.and remained there
for two and a half years, at the end of which time I went to
the Keh Kwang School on Avenue Road and after a further six
months study I graduated.

At this time fighting had broken out around Shanghai and I
returned to the home of my parents at Nanzing and stayed there
until about April 1938 when I and the entire family came to
Shanghai and took up residence at No 3 Chang Feng Li Nyburgh
Road. About a month later I entered the Great China University
and recommenced my studies and am at present still studying
therein.

Regarding my connection with my brother having
embezzled $40,000.00 from his employers, I wish to state as
follows; On October 17th 1938 I received a telephone call from
pages.zh:
顾家声（Kee Kya Tseong），别名小P宝（Siau Poh）
南京。D.S. Rhodes
总部 1938年10月19日 C.D.S. 273号。

我叫顾家声，别名小P宝，现年20岁，籍贯南京，现居住于勃伦南路（Brenan Road）长风里63号。

我出生于南京，当时我的父亲是杭州一家当铺的老板。八岁时，我开始在南京的一所名为“S Ngih”的小学校读书，并一直读到十二岁。

从十二岁到十四岁，我在南京中学就读，随后转入同样位于南京的同文中学（Tung Wee Middle School），在那里一直读到十六岁。离开该校后，我和名叫顾恺中（Kee Ts Tseeng）的哥哥来到上海，进入位于法租界霞飞路的青年中学（Tsing Nan / Young Men's High School），在那里读了两年半。之后，我转入爱文义路（Avenue Road）的光华大学附属中学（Keh Kwang School），又学习了六个月后毕业。

此时，上海周边爆发了战事，我回到南京父母家中，一直住到1938年4月左右，当时我和全家来到上海，居住在尼伯格路（Nyburgh Road）长风里3号。大约一个月后，我进入大夏大学重新开始学业，目前仍在那里就读。

关于我哥哥从其雇主处侵吞40,000.00美元一案中与我的牵连，我愿陈述如下：1938年10月17日，当我还在大学时，接到了他的电话，

pages.en:
2

him whilst I was at the University asking me to meet him out-
side the office of the Central Savings Society No 2 Tientsin
Road, I agreed and arrived there at about 12.30.pm., My
brother was just leaving the office of the C.S.S. at the time
in company with one named Yuen Ping Shing ( 袁炳生 ) who I
knew as a former school mate, my brother I noticed was carrying
a parcel in his hand and he told me that same contained money
and that he would explain every-thing later.

Leaving Tientsin Road we three, that is, my brother, Yuen
Ping Shing and myself, hired a Jenson car and proceeded to No
Liang Nyi Ling off Great Western Road which premises I knew to
be occupied by the brother of Yuen Ping Shing. We all entered
the house and my brother asked for writing paper and when this
was produced he sat down and commenced to write a note to one
named Per ( 潘 ), who this person was I did not at this time
know. My brother continued with the note and I saw that it was
in the form of an apology for having taken money, when complete
he placed the note in an envelope together with two cheques and
sealed it up. From the trend of the letter I more or less formed
my own opinion as to how my brother had come by so much money,
although at this stage he did not tell me any details.

After a lapse of about one hour we three hired a Ford car and
proceeded to the Weida Hotel Avenue Joffre F.C. and my brother
engaged room No 410, here he explained that because of
financial difficulties he had embezzled the money from his
employer and that after he had liquidated his debts he intended
to leave Shanghai and go first to Hongkong.
pages.zh:
2

他让我在天津路2号中央储蓄会办公室外与他见面，我同意了，并于下午12:30左右到达那里。当时我哥哥正与一名叫袁炳生（Yuen Ping Shing）的人一起离开中央储蓄会办公室，据我所知，袁是我以前的同学。我注意到我哥哥手里拿着一个包裹，他告诉我里面装的是钱，并说稍后会解释一切。

离开天津路后，我们三人，即我哥哥、袁炳生和我，雇了一辆詹森（Jenson）牌汽车，前往大西路附近的良友里（Liang Nyi Ling）某号，我知道该处由袁炳生的哥哥居住。我们都进了屋，我哥哥要了信纸，拿到后便坐下开始给一个叫潘（Per）的人写便条，当时我并不知道此人是谁。我哥哥继续写信，我看到信的内容大致是为拿钱一事表示歉意，写完后他将便条连同两张支票放入信封并封好。从信件的大致内容来看，我对哥哥如何得到这么多钱形成了自己的看法，尽管在此阶段他并未告诉我任何细节。

大约过了一个小时，我们三人雇了一辆福特汽车，前往法租界霞飞路的伟达饭店（Weida Hotel），我哥哥开了410号房间。在这里，他解释说由于财务困难，他从雇主那里侵吞了这笔钱，并打算在还清债务后离开上海，先去香港。

pages.en:
-3-

Before leaving the Weida Hotel he handed the letter he had
written at Great Western Road and asked me to deliver it to the
person Per ( 潘 ) at the Consolidated Tax Bureau 230
Kukiang Road, he also handed me $800.00 cash and requested me
to utilise same in liquidating his outstanding debts.
I took the letter and the cash and promised to do as directed
and he further asked that I would not inform my parents of his
behaviour, this I also promised and I left the Hotel promising
to return and visit him when I had carried out his
instructions. Upon leaving the hotel I first went to a small
hospital where I had cholera injections and then I went home.
The letter I placed in a book in my room and the cash I hid under
the pillow, intending to dispose of it as directed by my
brother later. Of the $800.00 cash I took $55.00 and redeemed
some clothing from pawn.

Later that same afternoon two male Chinese members of
the Consolidated Tax Bureau came to my home and questioned me
regarding the whereabouts of my brother, I declined to give
them any information whatsoever and finally I agreed to
accompany them to their office where I was subsequently I was
handed over to the Police, to whom I gave full particulars
regarding what had transpired between myself and my brother
and also his whereabouts.
The cheques and the cash were subsequently found in my room
where I had previously placed them. Although I was aware
that my brother had incurred debts I was unaware of his
contemplated action in regards to the method he intended to
pages.zh:
-3-

在离开伟达饭店之前，他交给我他在大西路写的信，让我交给九江路230号统税局的一个姓潘（Per）的人。他还交给我800.00美元现金，请求我用这笔钱偿还他的未清债务。
我接过信和现金，答应照办。他还要求我不要将他的行为告知父母，我也答应了。离开饭店时，我承诺在执行完他的指示后会回去看望他。离开饭店后，我先去了一家小医院注射霍乱疫苗，然后回家。我把信放在房间的一本书里，把现金藏在枕头下，打算稍后按哥哥的指示处理。在那800.00美元现金中，我取了55.00美元去当铺赎回了一些衣物。

当天下午晚些时候，两名中国籍的统税局男职员来到我家，询问我哥哥的下落。我拒绝向他们提供任何信息，最后我同意随他们去他们的办公室。随后我被移交给警方，我向警方详细说明了我和哥哥之间发生的一切以及他的下落。
支票和现金后来在我之前放置它们的房间里被找到。虽然我知道我哥哥欠了债，但我不知道他打算采用何种方法来筹集资金。

pages.en:
-4-

employ to raise the money.
I have absolutely no knowledge whatsoever regarding the
attempt on the life of Tzu Shih Chion (          ).
I have never been a member of any Political party and have
no interests in any such organizations, neither xx have I at
any time served in the Army.
To the best of my knowledge mybrother has no interests in
any political party.

This is my true statement.
Signed.
pages.zh:
-4-

对于刺杀邹志全（Tzu Shih Chion）（原文不清）的企图，我绝对一无所知。
我从未加入过任何政党，对任何此类组织都没有兴趣，我也从未在军队服役。
据我所知，我哥哥对任何政党都没有兴趣。

这是我的真实陈述。
签名。

pages.en:
Yuan Su Gee (袁世其) alias Yuan Ping Shing
Kiangsu                                      D.S. Rhodes
C 8,C.B.H.Q.          19-10-38               D.S.I. Wong Foh Sung

My name is Yuan Su Gee (袁世其), alias Yuan Ping Shing
(袁坏鑫). I am 19 years of age, single, native of Kiangsu,
and at present employed at the Central Savings Society, No.2
Tientsin Road and resident at No.60 Lane 633 Hart Road.
    I was born at Hoo Kiang, Kiangsu Province where my father
was at that time the owner of a large paper business. At the
age of five years I commenced school attending the Soo Jing (苏
群) primary school and studied therein for 6 years, after
which I removed to the Nanxing Middle School. Whilst at this
school one of my school mates was one Koo Ts Tsoong. When I was
14 years old I came to Shanghai and entered the S Poh Middle
School, Chapei and remained there for two years and then removed
to the Tsing Nan (青年) (Young Mens' High School), Avenue
Joffre where I again met my old school mate Koo Ts Tsoong (顾治中
his young brother Koo Kya Tsoong (顾家中) was also a student
at the same school. At this school I undertook a commercial
course and at the age of 18 graduated and returned to the home
of my parents. About April, 1937 I returned to Shanghai and
through the introduction of my uncle named Tsung Kyi Loh (沈嘉洛
I secured a position as a clerk in the receipts department of the
Central Savings Society, No.2 Tientsin Road.
    About two months ago my father, mother and all the family
came to Shanghai and took up residence at No.1 Liang Nyi Li off
Great Western Road.
    After taking up my position in the Central Savings Society
I frequently met Koo Ts Tsoong. At about 12.30 p.m. October
17th. 1938 Koo Ts Tsoong came to the Central Savings Society
pages.zh:
袁世其（Yuan Su Gee），别名袁坏鑫（Yuan Ping Shing，音译）
江苏                                      D.S. Rhodes
C 8, 中央捕房总部          1938年10月19日               D.S.I. 黄福松（Wong Foh Sung）

我叫袁世其，别名袁坏鑫。我今年19岁，未婚，籍贯江苏，目前在天津路2号中央储蓄会任职，居住在哈同路（Hart Road）633弄60号。
我出生于江苏省胡江（Hoo Kiang，音译），当时我父亲是一家大型纸业公司的老板。五岁时，我开始上学，就读于苏群（Soo Jing）小学，在那里学习了6年，之后转入南星中学（Nanxing Middle School）。在这所学校期间，我的同学之一是顾治中（Koo Ts Tsoong）。十四岁时，我来到上海，进入闸北的斯波中学（S Poh Middle School，音译），在那里待了两年，然后转入霞飞路的青年中学（Tsing Nan / Young Mens' High School），在那里我又遇到了老同学顾治中，他的弟弟顾家中（Koo Kya Tsoong，音译）也是同一所学校的学生。在这所学校，我修习商业课程，十八岁时毕业并回到父母家中。大约在1937年4月，我回到上海，通过叔叔沈嘉洛（Tsung Kyi Loh，音译）的介绍，我在天津路2号中央储蓄会的收款部谋得了一份职员的工作。
大约两个月前，我的父母和全家人来到上海，居住在大西路附近的良友里（Liang Nyi Li）1号。
在中央储蓄会任职后，我经常见到顾治中。1938年10月17日下午12:30左右，顾治中来到中央储蓄会

pages.en:
(2)

Office and informed me that he had important business he wished
to discuss with me and asked me to accompany him. We left the
building together and upon reached the roadway we were met by
Koo's young brother Koo Kya Tsoong (顧家忠). I asked the
nature of the important business and Koo asked if we could go to
Great Western Road the home of my brother and there he could
explain everything, I agreed and we hired a Johnson's car at
Peking Road and proceeded to that address.

Here we alighted paid the car fare and entered No.1 Liang
Nyi Li, Great Western Road, my brother was absent at the time
of our arrival, but my mother and father were present, I asked
them to wait in another room, when I returned Koo Ts Tsoong was
writing a note and I noticed that he was recording numbers and
also an amount of money, I asked what it was all about and he
replied that he was returning money to some one and that he
would explain everything later.

At about 1.30 p.m. I intimated that I must return to the
office whereupon Koo asked where he could go and after a few
minutes he finally decided on the Weida Hotel, we three took
a Ford Hire Car and at once proceeded to the Weida Hotel where
Koo Ts Tsoong engaged room No.410.

Here I again asked Koo the reason for his strange behaviour
and he explained how that morning he had embezzled $40,000.00
from his employer in order to liquidate certain outstanding
debts and that it was his intention to leave Shanghai and go to
Hongkong.

It was almost 5 o'clock by this time and I had to return
pages.zh:
(2)

办公室，告诉我他有重要事务想与我商议，并请我陪同他。我们一起离开大楼，走到路上时，遇到了顾的弟弟顾家忠（Koo Kya Tsoong）。我询问重要事务的性质，顾问我们能否去大西路我哥哥家，他可以在那里解释一切，我同意了。我们在北京路雇了一辆约翰逊（Johnson's）牌汽车，前往该地址。

在这里，我们下车付了车费，进入大西路良友里1号。我们到达时我哥哥不在，但我父母在家。我请他们在另一个房间等候。当我回来时，顾治中正在写便条，我注意到他记录了一些数字和一笔金额。我问这是怎么回事，他回答说他在把钱还给某人，稍后会解释一切。

下午1:30左右，我表示必须回办公室，于是顾问可以去哪里，几分钟后他最终决定去伟达饭店。我们三人坐了一辆福特租赁汽车，立即前往伟达饭店，顾治中开了410号房间。

在这里，我再次询问顾行为怪异的原因，他解释说当天早上为了偿还某些未清债务，他从雇主那里侵吞了40,000.00美元，并打算离开上海去香港。

此时已接近5点钟，我必须返回

pages.en:
(3)

to the office and when I informed Koo that I must leave he
asked me if I would take care of a parcel of the money for him,
he explaining that he did not think it safe to keep it in the
hotel, I promised and he gave me the money which was already
wrapped in a parcel , and before leaving he asked me to see
him again the same evening after leaving the office. (I was not
aware of the amount of money contained in this parcel). Having
to
no particular place to keep the money, I took it the Central
Savings Society with me and there without the knowledge of any
of the staff placed it in a safe drawer.

At about 7 p.m. the same evening I returned to the Weida
Hotel and again met Koo, he appeared to be very upset and again
said that he was leaving Shanghai soon and added that I should
phone him the following morning and he would make some arrange-
ments to collect the money he had given me to look after.

Before leaving the hotel at about 9 p.m. Koo asked me if
I could look after a further parcel of money for him and I
agreed, he then opened the parcel he had intimated he wished
me to take care of and I found that it contained $1,450.00.

Owing to the late hour I could not place this parcel in the
Central Savings Society so I took it home and put it in a
wardrobe in my room at No.60 Heng Tuh Li, Hart Road and then
went to bed.

Later the same evening detectives visited my home and when
questioned I related what had transpired between myself and
Koo Ta Tseong, later led them to the Central Savings Society
from where the parcel of money was recovered.
pages.zh:
(3)

办公室。当我告诉顾我必须离开时，他问我是否愿意帮他保管一包钱，他解释说他认为把钱放在饭店不安全。我答应了，他把已经包好的钱交给我。离开前，他让我下班后当晚再去看他。（我不知道这包里有多少钱）。由于没有特别的地方存放这笔钱，我把它带回中央储蓄会，并在没有任何职员知晓的情况下，将其放入保险柜抽屉中。

当晚7点左右，我回到伟达饭店，再次见到顾。他显得非常不安，再次说他很快就要离开上海，并补充说我应该在第二天早上给他打电话，他会安排取回我代为保管的钱。

当晚9点左右离开饭店前，顾问我是否能再帮他保管一包钱，我同意了。然后他打开他表示希望我保管的那个包裹，我发现里面装有1,450.00美元。

由于时间已晚，我无法将这包钱放入中央储蓄会，所以我把它带回家，放在哈同路恒德里（Heng Tuh Li，音译）60号我房间的衣柜里，然后上床睡觉。

当晚晚些时候，侦探来到我家。在接受询问时，我叙述了我和顾大钟（Koo Ta Tseong，音译，注：此处原文名字拼写与前文Goo/Koo Ts Tsoong略有不同，依原文译出）之间发生的事情。随后，我带领他们前往中央储蓄会，从那裡追回了那包钱。

pages.en:
(4)

Although a friend of Koo's prior to the embezzlement I
had no knowledge of his contemplated action, neither am I aware
of his personal affairs.
I have no interest in any political party and am not a
member of any such society.
Regarding the attempted assassination of Zau Shih Chuen I
have absolutely no knowledge or connection.
This is my true statement.

Sgd. Yuan Su Gee
pages.zh:
(4)

虽然在侵吞发生之前我是顾的朋友，但我对他预谋的行动一无所知，也不了解他的个人事务。
我对任何政党都没有兴趣，也不是任何此类社团的成员。
关于刺杀邹志全（Zau Shih Chuen）的企图，我绝对不知情，也无任何牵连。
这是我的真实陈述。

签名：袁世其

pages.en:
Yau Sung Sz (姚沈氏)
Soochow D.S. Fowler
C.B.H.Q.(C 8) 20-10-38 C. D. C. 31

My name is Yau Sung Sz (姚沈氏), age 23, native of Soochow,
divorcee, residing No.73/74 Bubbling Well Terrace, Bubbling Well
Road. I am working as a dancing hostess at the Paramount Ballroom
I was born in Soochow on the 15th. day of the 7th. month
1916. I married Yau Yue Hien (姚岳賢) in Soochow when I was
18. We were divorced in February 1937.
I have known Koo Ts Tsoong (顧治中) for about three months.
We met through the introduction of my ex-husband who sometimes
visits me to see our son, aged 4. Koo also accompanied him to
my home on occasions. I obtained my job as dance hostess through
the help of Koo Ts Tsoong who knew friends who were able to assist
him.
At about 10 p.m. on the 16th. October Koo and Yau came to my
home and Koo, because he said he was feeling depressed asked me
to accompany him and Yau to the Sun Co. dance hall to liven him
up a little. Whilst we were sitting at a table Koo passed a
remark that, "May be tomorrow I won't be here!" I asked him "Why?"
and he replied that he had had trouble with workers in the office
where he is employed and did not wish to continue working there.
I asked him where he proposed going and he told me "Chungking".
We danced together and at about 12 midnight left and the three
of us returned to our respective homes.
At about 3 p.m. on the 17th. October (next day) Koo Ts Tsoong
telephoned me at my home and asked me to meet him at a room
(number forgotten but it was situated on the 4th. floor) in
Weida Hotel, Avenue Joffre, French Concession. He did not mention
why he wished to see me. I left my home and proceeded by ricksha
to the hotel in question.
pages.zh:
姚沈氏 (Yau Sung Sz)
苏州。D.S. Fowler 警官。
中央捕房总部 (C 8) 1938年10月20日 C. D. C. 31

我叫姚沈氏，23岁，苏州人，离异，现居静安寺路静安别墅73/74号。我在百乐门舞厅担任舞女。
我于1916年农历七月十五日出生于苏州。18岁时在苏州与姚岳賢 (Yau Yue Hien) 结婚。我们于1937年2月离婚。
我认识顾治中 (Koo Ts Tsoong) 大约三个月了。我们是经我的前夫介绍认识的，他有时来看望我们要4岁的儿子。顾治中也曾几次陪同前夫来我家。我是通过顾治中的帮助才得到这份舞女工作的，他认识一些能帮上忙的朋友。
10月16日晚上10点左右，顾治中和姚岳賢来到我家，顾治中说因为心情郁闷，让我陪他和姚岳賢去新仙林舞厅散散心。当我们坐在桌旁时，顾治中说了一句：“也许明天我就不在这里了！”我问他“为什么？”，他回答说他在受雇的办公室里与工人发生了纠纷，不想继续在那里工作。我问他打算去哪里，他告诉我“重庆”。我们一起跳了舞，大约在午夜12点离开，我们三人各自回家。
第二天，即10月17日下午3点左右，顾治中在我家给我打电话，约我在法租界霞飞路伟达酒店的一个房间见面（房间号忘了，但在四楼）。他没有提及为何要见我。我离开家，乘黄包车前往该酒店。

pages.en:
(2)

On reaching the room I was met by Koo, the only occupant
who ordered food for both of us. During the meal Koo said he
was leaving Shanghai and was possibly going to Chungking. He
also said that he had wanted to buy a present for me before but
had been unable to do so because of financial difficulties.
However, he had "squeezed" some money from the office and handed
me $200.00 in notes and asked me to accept it and buy something
for myself. I demurred but he insisted I take it for friendship's
sake. I accepted the money and, after thanking him, left the room
and returned home at about 4 p.m.

At about 5 p.m. detectives from Central Station came to my
home and asked me if I knew the man depicted on a small photograph
The man was Koo and I replied that I knew him and was a friend of
his. I was told he had stolen $40,000.00 and then asked if I
knew where he was at that time. I pleaded ignorance, because I
thought that if Koo was located and action taken against him I
should also be in trouble for accepting $200.00 from him.

The detectives on leaving left a card with me saying that if
I learned where Koo was I was to telephone them.

At about 6.30 p.m. my ex-husband's brother Yau Yah Ngoo
telephoned me say Yau (my ex-husband) had been arrested for
"squeezing" money from his office and asked me to go to his home,
~~Lane 74 House 63 North Thibet Road.~~ On going there at about
9 p.m. he asked me if I knew where Koo Ta Tsoong was as he was
the one who had stolen the $40,000.00, I again denied knowledge
of his whereabouts. I returned home at about 10.15 p.m.

At about 2 a.m. on the 18-10-38 detectives came to my home
pages.zh:
(2)

到达房间后，顾治中接待了我，他是房间里唯一的人，并为我们两人点了食物。用餐期间，顾治中说他要离开上海，可能去重庆。他还说以前想给我买份礼物，但因为经济困难没能买成。然而，他从办公室“挤”出了一些钱，递给我200.00元钞票，让我收下并给自己买点东西。我推辞了，但他坚持为了友谊让我收下。我收下了钱，向他道谢后离开房间，大约在下午4点回到家。

下午5点左右，中央捕房的侦探来到我家，问我是否认识一张小照片上描绘的男子。那个人是顾治中，我回答说我认识他，并且是他的朋友。他们告诉我他偷了40,000.00元，然后问我当时是否知道他在哪里。我声称不知情，因为我想如果顾治中被找到并受到制裁，我也会因为收了他200.00元而惹上麻烦。

侦探离开时留给我一张名片，说如果我得知顾治中的下落，就给他们打电话。

晚上6点半左右，我前夫的弟弟姚梧 (Yau Yah Ngoo) 给我打电话，说姚岳賢（我的前夫）因从办公室“挤”钱被捕，并叫我去他家，~~西藏北路74弄63号。~~ 晚上9点左右到了那里后，他问我是否知道顾大忠 (Koo Ta Tsoong) 在哪里，因为是他偷了那40,000.00元，我再次否认知道他的下落。我于晚上10点15分左右回到家。

1938年10月18日凌晨2点左右，侦探来到我家

pages.en:
(3)

and took me into custody as a result of Koo having been arrested.
I also handed the $200.00 I had received from Koo to the detec-
tives.
    I do not know anything further regarding the theft.
    The foregoing is a true statement.

                    Signed. Yau Sung Sz
pages.zh:
(3)

并将我拘留，这是顾治中被捕的结果。我也将从顾治中那里收到的200.00元交给了侦探。
    关于这起盗窃案，我不知道更多情况。
    以上陈述属实。

                    签名：姚沈氏

pages.en:
Yau Yue Yuen(姚子儀)alias Zung Ts. 潤芝
Soochow.                                      D.S. Fowler.
C.B.H.Q.(C.S)             19-10-38.

My name is Yau Yue Yien(姚子儀), age 26, native of
Soochow, M/accountant, residing Lane 88, House 104 Connaught
Road.
    I was born on Dec. 10, 1913 in Soochow. I have a mother
and brother, Yau Yah Ngoo(姚梧), both residing Lane 74
House 63 North Thibet Road.
    I am at present working as an accountant in the Consolidated
Tax Bureau(under Japanese Supervision)at No. 230 Kiukiang
Road and have been so employed for the past nine months. My
salary is $110.00 per month.
    At the age of 7 years I attended the Tsung Sung(泰申)
Primary School in Soochow and stayed there until I was 11 years
old. I next attended the Soo Tuh(樹德)Advanced Primary
School in Soochow and stayed until I was 14 years of age. I
then attended the Yih Tsung(義成)Middle School, in Soochow
until I was 17.
    On leaving the last school, I went to work as a clerk
for one named Ts Tsung Yoch(朱承鉞)a lawyer in Soochow and
stayed for over one year.
    I next worked as assistant accountant at the Soochow
Development Bank(中國興業銀行). After being so employed
for one year the bank closed its doors. I was then 19.
    My mother and I then opened a general stores in Soochow
and I continued in this business for 2 years when, due to trade
depression the shop was closed. It was during this period I
married my wife Sung Hwo Ying(沈煥英). I then opened another
small general store myself and operated it for about 1½ years.
pages.zh:
姚子儀 (Yau Yue Yuen)，别名润芝 (Zung Ts)。
苏州。                                      D.S. Fowler 警官。
中央捕房总部 (C.S)             1938年10月19日。

我叫姚子儀 (Yau Yue Yien)，26岁，苏州人，会计师，现居康纳特路88弄104号。
    我于1913年12月10日出生于苏州。我有母亲和兄弟姚梧 (Yau Yah Ngoo)，他们都居住在西藏北路74弄63号。
    我目前在九江路230号的统税局（在日本人监管下）担任会计师，已任职九个月。我的月薪是110.00元。
    我7岁时进入苏州的泰申 (Tsung Sung) 小学就读，一直读到11岁。接着我进入苏州的树德 (Soo Tuh) 高等小学，一直读到14岁。随后我进入苏州的义成 (Yih Tsung) 中学，一直读到17岁。
    离开最后一所学校后，我去苏州给一位名叫朱承鉞 (Ts Tsung Yoch) 的律师当职员，干了一年多。
    接着我在苏州兴业银行 (Soochow Development Bank) 担任助理会计师。在那里工作一年后，银行倒闭了。那时我19岁。
    随后我和母亲在苏州开了一家杂货店，我继续经营这项生意2年，后来由于商业萧条，店铺关闭了。正是在这段时期，我与妻子沈煥英 (Sung Hwo Ying) 结婚。之后我自己又开了一家小杂货店，经营了大约一年半。

pages.en:
- 2 -

I again lost my money. For the next two years I stayed at home
and then, when 25, I came to Shanghai with my mother, brother
and his wife relatives in Nov.1937 and lived in No. 5 Hoo Foh
Loong off Nanking Road the home of a friend. The reason of
our coming to Shanghai was due to the Sino-Japanese hostilities
I assisted my friend Ling Kya Pau(凌嘉宝)in the Cotton
business until January 1938 when I was successful in obtaining
my present position. I moved to the Connaught Road address in
June.
Regarding the case concerning Koo Ts Tsoong(顾治中), in
which is involved a sum of $40,000.00. I have known Koo Ts
Tsoong only since I have worked in the Consolidated Tax
Bureau. He occupies the desk opposite mine in the office.
During leisure hours I have, on occasions, gone to dance
halls with him. One day about two weeks ago(about 3rd or 4th
October)I went with Koo Ts Tsoong and a mutual friend also
working in the office, Pau Liang Tsoo(潘良佐)to the Wei Koeng
(偉宮)Dance Hall, Ningpo Road during the tiffin hour.
The three of us had food and during which Koo Ts Tsoong
mentioned that he was financially embarrassed due to his keeping
company with a female and the other little things one likes which
are not an actual necessity. He mentioned that things were
really serious and he owed about $700 or $800 and that being
as he did not know how to settle the debts it would probably
be better for him to commit suicide. This brought forth a
reply in a joking manner from Pau Liang Tsoo that he ought not
to worry as he was working among money and he could very easily
pick up some. Koo only smiled in reply. Nothing further was
mentioned regarding the debts or money to be obtained.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

我又亏了钱。接下来的两年我待在家里，然后在25岁时，也就是1937年11月，我和母亲、兄弟及其妻室亲戚一起来到上海，住在南京路附近胡福龙 (Hoo Foh Loong) 5号的一位朋友家里。我们来上海的原因是由于中日敌对行动。
    我协助我的朋友凌嘉宝 (Ling Kya Pau) 做棉花生意，直到1938年1月，我成功获得了现在的职位。我在6月搬到了康纳特路的地址。
    关于涉及40,000.00元金额的顾治中 (Koo Ts Tsoong) 案件。我自从在统税局工作以来才认识顾治中。他在办公室里坐在我对面的办公桌。
    在闲暇时间，我偶尔会和他一起去舞厅。大约两周前的一天（大约10月3日或4日），我和顾治中以及另一位也在办公室工作的共同朋友潘良佐 (Pau Liang Tsoo) 在午餐时间去宁波路的伟宫 (Wei Koeng) 舞厅。
    我们三人吃了饭，期间顾治中提到，因为与一名女性交往，以及一些并非真正必需的个人喜好开销，导致他经济窘迫。他提到情况真的很严重，他欠了大约700或800元，由于不知道如何偿还债务，最好还是自杀算了。对此，潘良佐开玩笑地回答说他不应该担心，因为他是在钱堆里工作，很容易就能弄到一些钱。顾治中只是笑了笑作为回应。关于债务或搞钱的事，没有再提其他内容。

pages.en:
- 3 -

At about 7 p.m. on the 9th or 10th of October, Koo Ts Tsoong
went to my home in Connaught Road and spoke again of owing money
and also that he had given thought to the joking suggestion of
Pau Liang Tsoo and that he had decided to steal money from the
office. I replied that the office was under the Japanese and
should he steal some money from there there would undoubtedly
be trouble for his parents and relatives. Also, should he steal
the money and be caught later, the Japanese would probably
shoot him. I further explained that although $800.00 or $900.00
was a lot of money he ought to go and explain the whole situation
to his father who might then assist him and the trouble would
be over. He stated he definitely would not mention anything to
his father or ask for money.

As he appeared determined on stealing money from the office,
I asked him what he was going to do after the theft and he
replied that he would pay off his debts and make his way to
Chungking. I also asked him how much he intended stealing and
was informed that he thought about $3,000.00 or $4,000.00
would suffice. After a talk on various other subjects he
returned to his home.

On attending office the following morning, and subsequent
mornings, I noticed that he wore a somewhat despondent expression
but I did not speak to him of it neither, as far as I know, did
anyone else.

At about 7 p.m. on the 16th October Koo Ts Tsoong went to my home
and he, my wife and I had the evening meal together. He was very
depressed and openly expressed the fact and asked my wife and I
pages.zh:
- 3 -

10月9日或10日晚上7点左右，顾治中来到我在康纳特路的家中，再次谈到欠钱的事，还说他已经考虑过潘良佐那个玩笑般的建议，并决定从办公室偷钱。我回答说办公室是在日本人管辖之下，如果他从那里面偷钱，无疑会给他的父母和亲戚带来麻烦。而且，如果他偷了钱后来被抓，日本人可能会枪毙他。我进一步解释说，虽然800.00或900.00元是一笔大钱，但他应该去向他父亲解释整个情况，他父亲可能会帮助他，这样麻烦就结束了。他表示绝对不会向他父亲提及此事或要钱。

由于他似乎决心要从办公室偷钱，我问他偷窃后打算做什么，他回答说他会还清债务，然后前往重庆。我还问他打算偷多少，被告知他认为大约3,000.00或4,000.00元就足够了。在谈论了其他各种话题后，他回自己家去了。

第二天早上及随后的几个早上上班时，我注意到他面带愁容，但我没有跟他提起，据我所知，其他人也没有。

10月16日晚上7点左右，顾治中来到我家，他、我妻子和我一起吃晚饭。他非常沮丧，并公开表达了这一点，请求我妻子和我

pages.en:
- 4 -

to accompany him to a dance hall to try and liven him up a
little. The three of us went to the Sun Company dance hall at
about 9 p.m. and stayed until 11 p.m.

Whilst the three of us were sitting at a table in the dance
hall Koo, who still was very depressed, passed the remark that
"May be tomorrow I shan't be here." I thought he meant he
would commit suicide but I did not speak. My wife apparently
thought he meant suicide because she said, "Oh! You musn't
commit suicide," whereupon Koo replied that he did not intend
doing so.

A few minutes later Koo and I were alone and I, remembering
his previous remark re stealing money, asked him how he was
going away if he hadn't money and didn't intend committing
suicide. He did not reply. I reminded him of his previous remark
re stealing money from the office but he assured me that he did not
intend so doing. To try and impress him of the seriousness
of the offence I told him that should he steal money from the
office and I knew that he was the culprit, I would inform my
superiors. We left the dance hall a short time later.

The following morning(17th October) I was at the office at
9 a.m. but Koo Ts Tseong did not put in an appearance until
10 a.m. I spoke to him re the time and he replied that he had
overslept. At about 11.45 a.m. I noticed Koo's absence and
asked a teaboy if he had seen him and received the reply Koo
had gone. I thought no more of it and went home at 12 noon.

On attending the office at 2 p.m. Koo was still absent.

At 2.15 p.m. I heard Pau Liang Tsoo telephone downstairs
pages.zh:
- 4 -

陪他去舞厅，试着让他振作一点。我们三人大约在晚上9点去了新仙林舞厅，一直待到晚上11点。

当我们在舞厅坐在桌旁时，仍然非常沮丧的顾治中说了一句：“也许明天我就不在这里了。”我以为他的意思是要自杀，但我没说话。我妻子显然也以为他是指自杀，因为她说：“哦！你不能自杀，”于是顾治中回答说他并不打算这样做。

几分钟后，只剩下顾治中和我两个人，我想起他之前关于偷钱的言论，便问他如果没有钱又不打算自杀，他怎么离开。他没有回答。我提醒他之前关于从办公室偷钱的言论，但他向我保证他不打算这样做。为了让他意识到罪行的严重性，我告诉他，如果他从办公室偷钱，而我知道他是罪犯，我会向上级报告。不久后我们离开了舞厅。

第二天早上（10月17日），我上午9点在办公室，但顾治中 (Koo Ts Tseong) 直到上午10点才出现。我就时间问题跟他说了几句，他回答说睡过头了。大约上午11点45分，我注意到顾治中不在，就问一个茶房是否见过他，得到的回答是顾治中已经走了。我没再多想，中午12点回家了。

下午2点到办公室时，顾治中仍然缺席。

下午2点15分，我听到潘良佐在楼下打电话

pages.en:
- 5 -

and ask for the money and cheques which had been paid in during
the morning. A few minutes later Hyleu Ping San(徐炳燧)
in charge of the office downstairs, came upstairs with the
money. I heard him telling Pau Liang Tsoo that Koo Ts Tsoong
had taken a cheque for $40,000.00 at 11.30 a.m. and had signed
a receipt for it. This was produced. Pau Liang Tsoo denied
sending Koo for money or knowing he had taken it. It was then
generally discovered that Koo was not present in the office.

The cheque having been drawn on the National Commercial
Bank, a call was put through asking re the cheque. It was
learned it had been cashed at about 11.30 a.m.

The drawer in Koo's desk was broken open by Pau Liang Tsoo
and in it was found two letters, one addressed to myself and
the other to Zau Tai Ts(趙淡是), the Manager's brother.

As a result of a telephone call made to his home, Zau Tai
Ts attended the office at about 3.15 p.m. and was handed the
letter addressed to him and I was given the one addressed to me.

A translation of my letter reads:-

To Zung Ts:-

It is too late for me to regret not having accepted yours
advice; however I will not commit suicide. I will not be so
hard-hearted as to abandon a pregnant girl. Poor "Yung Tsing"
for her I have decided to sacrifice everything, so don't think
I am mad.

I am sorry that I could not tell you about this occurrence
earlier but I believed you would prevent me from doing so. I
do not wish to let you know my present whereabouts until Yung
pages.zh:
- 5 -

询问上午存入的钱款和支票。几分钟后，负责楼下办公室的徐炳燧 (Hyleu Ping San) 拿着钱款上楼。我听到他告诉潘良佐，顾治中在上午11点30分拿走了一张40,000.00元的支票，并签收了收据。收据被出示了。潘良佐否认派顾治中去取钱或知道他拿走了钱。随后大家发现顾治中不在办公室。

由于支票是开给国家商业银行的，于是打电话查询该支票的情况。得知支票已在上午11点30分左右兑现。

潘良佐撬开了顾治中办公桌的抽屉，在里面发现了两封信，一封是写给我的，另一封是写给经理的兄弟赵淡是 (Zau Tai Ts) 的。

由于往他家打了一个电话，赵淡是在下午3点15分左右来到办公室，有人把写给他的信交给了他，我也拿到了写给我的那封信。

我收到的信的译文如下：

致润芝：

现在后悔没有接受你的建议已经太晚了；然而我不会自杀。我不会那么狠心抛弃一个怀孕的女孩。可怜的“永清” (Yung Tsing)，为了她我决定牺牲一切，所以不要以为我疯了。

很抱歉我不能早点告诉你这件事，但我相信你会阻止我这么做。在永清

pages.en:
- 6 -

Tsing's affair is settled. Maybe I shall leave Shanghai but
I'll inform you when doing so. Please convey my sorrow to Ming
Yuen.

Zau Tai Ts then questioned me re the letter I had received.
On his reading it he asked why I had not informed the office
of the contemplated theft. I explained as previously related
in this statement and denied knowing he was going to steal the
money. I and others were later taken to Central Police Station
for questioning(3.50p.m.)

Whilst in the station I heard that Zau Shih Chuen had been
shot at in his M/car by unknown persons. Inasmuch as I have not
left Central Station since being taken there at 3.50 p.m. on
the 17-10-38 for questioning re the theft of the cheque, I do
not know anything whatever regarding the attempted assassination.

The above is true.

Signed.
pages.zh:
- 6 -

赵（Tsing）的事已了结。我也许会离开上海，但届时我会通知你。请向明远（Ming Yuen）转达我的悲痛。

随后，邹泰茨（Zau Tai Ts，音译）就我收到的那封信对我进行了讯问。他读完信后问我，为何没有向局里报告这起预谋盗窃案。我作了如本陈述前文所述的解释，并否认知道他要偷钱。后来，我和其他人被带到中央捕房接受讯问（下午3点50分）。

在捕房期间，我听说邹世权（Zau Shih Chuen，音译）在其汽车内遭到不明身份者枪击。鉴于我自1938年10月17日下午3点50分因支票被盗一事被带往中央捕房接受讯问以来，一直未离开该处，因此我对这起暗杀未遂事件一无所知。

以上属实。

签名。

pages.en:
Pan Liang Tsu.
Ningpo.                                D.S.I. Crighton.
C.8.              18-10-38.

My name is Pan Liang Tsu(潘良佐). I am 26 years old,
a native of Ningpo, married Chief cashier, employed at the
Consolidated Tax Bureau, located at 230 Kiukiang Road, residing
at House 60, Lane 357, Weihaiwei Road. I am also a partner in
the Tien Fah Ziang(天發祥) Fur Shop, Honan Road.

I was born in Shanghai and at that time my father was a
fur merchant, being Manager of the Chuen Fah Yuen(全發源) Fur
Store, then located on Honan Road but now defunct.

Until I attained the age of 22 years I studied Commercial
Courses at the following Schools:- first, Shanghai Public School
for Chinese under Mr. Kemp, Fu Tan Experimental Middle School
under Sung Vaung Dau(孫鳳道), National Commercial Night
College under Zee Bei Wang(徐佩璜). Having completed my
studies I obtained a position in the American Engineering
Company as accountant and held this position until the end of
February 1938, when at the request of Mr. Chao Shih Chuen(趙式軍)
Director General of the Consolidated Tax Bureau, I accepted the
position of Chief cashier in this Bureau at a monthly salary
$200.00, plus $200.00 per monthly personal allowance.

Regarding the Embezzlement of $40,000.00 by one named Koo
Ts Tsoong(顧治中) I beg to state that at about 11 a.m. 17-10-38
one Mr. Sung Zung Fah(沈順福) an Inspector of the Bureau, came
and reported to me that my car had been slightly damaged whilst
standing on Kiukiang Road and that the Chinese Police Constable
had taken a wheel-barrow coolie to the Station in connection
with same. Intending to proceed to Central Station re this
accident I first instructed Mr. Zee Ping Zai(徐炳崽) a collector
pages.zh:
潘良佐。
宁波。                                D.S.I. Crighton.
C.8.              1938年10月18日。

我叫潘良佐。现年26岁，宁波人，已婚，任统税局首席出纳员。该局位于九江路230号，我居住在威海卫路357弄60号。我也是河南路天發祥皮货店的合伙人。

我出生于上海，当时家父是皮货商，担任全發源皮货店经理，该店当时位于河南路，现已歇业。

在我22岁之前，我在以下学校修习商业课程：首先是在肯普（Kemp，音译）先生执教下的上海公立华童公学；其次是在孙凤道执教下的复旦实验中学；再次是在徐佩璜执教下的国立商业夜校。学业完成后，我在美国工程公司获得会计师职位，并一直担任该职至1938年2月底。当时，应统税局总监赵式军先生的要求，我接受了该局首席出纳员的职位，月薪200.00元，另加每月个人津贴200.00元。

关于名为顾治中者侵吞40,000.00元一事，谨陈述如下：1938年10月17日上午11时许，该局督察沈顺福先生前来向我报告，称我的汽车停在九江路时受到轻微损坏，中国巡捕已就此事件将一名独轮车苦力带往捕房。我本打算前往中央捕房处理此事故，便先指示“收款部”的收款员徐炳崽先生，在我下午回来之前，不得向“出纳部”支付任何现金或支票。随后我前往中央捕房，在就事故作出报告后，我决定返回办公室，因为当时离午餐时间尚早。

pages.en:
- 2 -

in the "Collection Department," that he was not to hand out
any cash or cheques to the "Cashier Department" until I returned
in the afternoon. I then proceeded to the Central Police
Station where after making my report re the accident, I decided
to return to the office as it was then still early for Lunch.
Arriving at the door of the Tax Bureau, I met Marine Captain
Yang Su Tuh(楊基德)and three friends who invited me to lunch
at the Woo Faung Tsa(卫芳斋)Restaurant, Nanking Road near
Shanse Road. I accompanied them there and I had lunch together
which cost $1.76. Leaving there we next proceeded to the
Palis Cafe, Avenue Edward VII where on entering I met three
friends, all employees of the National City Bank. We remained
there until approximately 2 p.m. and I then returned to my
office arriving there shortly after 2 p.m. At about 2.30 p.m.
Mr. Zee Ping Zai(徐炳道)came to me from the Collection
Department and handed me a number of cheques, however, on
examining same I found a cheque for $40,000.00 missing and on
its place a receipt against Koo T~ Tseong(顧治中)who had drawn
same. I then enquired from Zee(徐 )what had happened and he
quite innocently explained that just prior to my departure at
11 a.m. that day Koo Ts Tseong(顧治中)had come to him and
asking what cash he had in hand explained that the "Cashier
Department" required a large amount urgently. Mr. Zee then
related how he explained to Koo(顧)that he had only $500.00 in
cash in hand, whereupon Koo(顧)stated that this amount was
insufficient and that the Department wanted a larger amount,
hence he(Zee) then showed him several cheques the largest amount
pages.zh:
- 2 -

到达统税局门口时，我遇见海军上尉杨基德和三位朋友，他们邀请我去南京路近山西路的卫芳斋餐馆吃午饭。我随同前往并共进午餐，花费1.76元。离开那里后，我们接着前往爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的Palis咖啡馆（音译），进门时我遇见了三位朋友，均为花旗银行职员。我们在那里逗留至下午2点左右，随后我返回办公室，于下午2点后不久抵达。下午2点30分左右，收款部的徐炳道先生来到我这里，交给我一些支票，然而经检查，我发现一张面额40,000.00元的支票不见了，取而代之的是一张由顾治中开具的收据。于是我向徐询问发生了什么事，他天真地解释说，就在当天上午11点我离开前不久，顾治中来找他，询问他手头有多少现金，并解释说“出纳部”急需一大笔款项。徐接着讲述了他如何向顾解释他手头只有500.00元现金，顾随即表示这笔金额不足，部门需要更大的金额，因此徐便向他出示了几张支票，最大面额

pages.en:
- 3 -

being for $3,000.00 and $40,000.00 respectively. The latter
cheque was a "Pay to bearer" cash cheque issued on the National
Commercial Bank by the Hwa Ching(華盛 )Tobacco Company and
Koo(顧 )stated that he would take that hence Zee had him sign
a receipt for same and handed same over to him. My suspicions
being aroused, I immediately telephoned to the National
Commercial Bank and was informed that the cheque in question
had been cashed. Fearing the worst I then went to Koo Ts Tsoong's
guarantor Mr. Har Ming Yuen(哈明遠)another cashier in the
department together we proceeded to the National Commercial Bank,
where we were informed the cheque had been cashed into $6,000.00
in cash and two cross cash orders on Native Banks for $4,000.00
and $30,000.00 respectively. I then returned to the office
and telephoned to Mr. Lai Tan Shu informing him of what had
happened and he promised to attend the office right away.
Having done this I next in the company of Mr. Chow Bai Long(邱培郎
introducer of Koo Ts Tsoong(顧治中 )proceeded to the home of
the latter at 63 Chamfoong Bei Se(兆丰别墅 )Brenan Road,
however on arrival there we failed to find him only his step
mother being present, and she could not assist us in any way,
leaving Mr. Chow Bai Long(邱培郎)in this house I went outside
for the purpose of telephoning the Bureau, however on gaining
the roadway I encountered the brother of Koo Ts Tsoong(顧治中)
who denied knowing the whereabouts of his brother. I then
requested him to go to the house and await my return, whilst I
went outside and telephone to Mr. Chee regarding the details of
my investigation so far. I then returned to the house of Mr
pages.zh:
- 3 -

分别为3,000.00元和40,000.00元。后一张支票是由华盛烟草公司在国家商业银行开出的“付持票人”现金支票，顾表示他要拿走这张支票，于是徐让他签了一张收据，并将支票交给了他。我心生疑窦，立即致电国家商业银行，得知该支票已被兑现。担心事态严重，我随即去找顾治中的担保人、同部门的另一名出纳员哈明远先生，我们一起前往国家商业银行，在那里获悉该支票已被兑换成6,000.00元现金，以及两张分别金额为4,000.00元和30,000.00元的钱庄交叉现金汇票。随后我返回办公室，打电话给赖坦舒（Lai Tan Shu，音译）先生告知发生的情况，他答应立刻来办公室。做完这些后，我与顾治中的介绍人邱培郎先生一同前往后者位于兆丰别墅布伦南路（Brenan Road，即今高安路）63号的住所，然而到达那里后我们未能找到他，只有他的继母在家，她无法提供任何帮助。我将邱培郎留在那所房子里，自己走到外面准备给局里打电话，然而刚走到路上，我就遇到了顾治中的兄弟，他否认知道其兄的下落。于是我要求他去屋里等候我回来，而我走到外面打电话给Chee先生（音译），汇报我目前的调查细节。随后我回到那所房子

pages.en:
- 4 -

and questioned his brother who stated that Koo had a girl friend
residing in Hwakee Avenue, but that he did not know the exact
address. On hearing this I suggested that we go to this
address and if necessary search every house and he agreed to
accompany me, however on the way I thought it would be better
to return to the Bureau and let the Police handle the case
from there on hence I made an excuse that probably Koo Ts Tsoong's
friend Yao You Hyi(姚予儀)would be able to locate this girl
and in this manner got Koo's brother to the Bureau, where we
met Mr. T.Thomas Cheque advisor to the Bureau, who recommended
that we all attend Central Police Station. Thus at 4 p.m.
we all proceeded to the aforesaid station where I related to
Mr. Dickson the aforegoings:-

Ques. How long have you known Koo Ts Tsoong(顧治中)?
Ans. He had joined the Tax Bureau before I had, therefore it was not
until I joined this organization that I became acquainted with
him.

Ques. Do you know how Koo Ts Tsoong came to join the Tax Bureau?
Ans. I know that his guarantors were Yao You Hyi(姚予儀)and Han Ming
Yuen(哈明遠), who had also joined the Bureau before I had.

Ques. Who introduced Koo Ts Tsoong to the Bureau?
Ans. He was introduced by Chow Bei Long(邱培郎)who is an employee
of the petty affairs division, and also I think a relative of
Koo's.

Ques. As you are Chief Cashier in the Bureau, what would you say
regarding the General Character of these persons mentioned above?
Ans. As far as I know these four men have very few outside companions,
pages.zh:
- 4 -

并讯问了他的兄弟，他说顾有一个女朋友住在华界大道（Hwakee Avenue，音译，或指华格理路/华山路等，此处依原文音译），但他不知道确切地址。听到这话，我建议我们去那个地址，必要时逐户搜查，他同意陪我前往，但在途中我想最好还是回局里，让警方从那里接手处理此案，因此我找了个借口，说顾治中的朋友姚予仪也许能找到这个女孩，就这样我把顾的兄弟带到了局里，在那里我们遇见了局里的支票顾问T. Thomas先生，他建议我们都去中央捕房。于是下午4点，我们全都前往上述捕房，我向迪克森（Dickson）先生陈述了上述经过：

问：你认识顾治中多久了？
答：他比我先进入统税局，因此直到我加入该机构后才与他相识。

问：你知道顾治中是如何进入统税局的吗？
答：我知道他的担保人是姚予仪和哈明远，他们也比我先进入该局。

问：是谁把顾治中介绍进局的？
答：他是被邱培郎介绍的，邱是杂务科的雇员，而且我想也是顾的亲戚。

问：既然你是局里的首席出纳员，你对上述这些人的总体品行有何看法？
答：据我所知，这四个人在外面的朋友很少，

pages.en:
- 5 -
but I am not in a position to give details regarding their
private lives, hence I would not incriminate myself so far.
To the best of your knowledge has Koo Ts Tseong(顧治中)ever
before attempted to embezzle monies from the Bureau.
To my knowledge this is the first time that he has done so.

Signed:
pages.zh:
- 5 -
但我无法提供有关他们私生活的细节，因此在此范围内我不会让自己陷入罪责。
据你所知，顾治中以前是否曾试图从局里侵吞款项？
据我所知，这是他第一次这样做。

签名：

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.

OCT 21 1939

Zau Takes Up
Residence In
Hongkew Area

Following the attempt on his life

SHANGHAI TIMES,
OCT 19 1938

Attempted Assassination Of Zau
Reveals Devilishly Clever Plot

Puppet Official Visits
Office Infrequently
And Irregularly
Always Changes Route,
But Gunmen Manage
To Keep Track

Details of the attempted assassination of Zau Sheh-kung, general director of the Nippon-sponsored "Consolidated Tax Bureau," Monday evening reveal that the attack was cunningly planned by men of superior intelligence.

Two gunmen, standing opposite Laou Kai Fook's Silk Store, Hardoon Building, blazed away at his glistening Buick limousine as it passed, traveling west at 5:15 p.m. Monday. Their bullets struck the car nine times, but Zau's heavy investment in the bullet-proof machine stood up under the test, and not a single bullet pierced the armored plate.

Zau, his personal assistant, a bodyguard and a chauffeur all escaped unscathed. The gunmen also disappeared, one of them first dumping his revolver between rolls of silk in Laou Kai Fook.

That the assassins were not greenhorns may be concluded from the fact that they did not fire a single shot at the windows of the car, taking it for granted that they would be bullet-proof. They were, for the glass in the windows was more than an inch thick.

Attack Well-Planned

The assassination must have been planned for days in advance in such a way as to make it foolproof, for Zau's visits to his office at 230 Kiukiang Road, Continental Bank Building, were infrequent and irregular. Only the armored plating saved his life, for the bullets were all aimed accurately, directly at the rear seat.

It was only by chance that Zau had gone to his office Monday. That afternoon he received a call on his personal phone at home, a phone which only he uses and few people know about, that there had been a $40,000 misappropriation in his office. He was asked to come down.

It is understood that he arrived there shortly after 3 p.m. He left again at approximately 5 o'clock, bound for his home at 39 Nanyang Road.

Zau usually made the trip by devious routes. His chauffeur has instructions never to stop for a traffic signal, but that if a red light should block a forward advance, then a left turn should be made.

Caught By Red Light

It so happened that traveling toward the Bund from the Continental Building, the car was caught at the Szechuen Road corner.

According to his instructions the chauffeur turned left, intending to turn right at Nanking Road and thus proceed to the Bund. However, at Nanking Road there was another red light, and he was again forced to turn left.

Thus it happened, by chance, that the car was on Nanking Road, heading west. Yet, when it approached the Honan Road intersection, only two blocks west, the car was fired on.

It is believed that there were more than two gunmen, that assassins were posted at all roads leading from the Continental Bank Building, and that lookouts were posted to inform the gunmen of the direction the car was taking.

Following Monday's shooting S.M. Police rounded up 12 suspects. The same day the majority of these were released, but the police are still carrying on investigations in connection with the remainder.

（批：Lil 8 19/10）

邹氏遇刺未遂案
揭露极其狡猾的阴谋

傀儡官员极少且
不规律地前往办公室
总是改变路线，
但枪手仍能
掌握其行踪

周一晚间发生的针对日本扶植的“统税局”总监邹世坤（Zau Sheh-kung，音译）的暗杀未遂事件详情显示，这次袭击是由高智商人士精心策划的。

周一傍晚5点15分，当邹那辆光亮的别克豪华轿车向西驶过时，两名站在哈同大楼老介福绸缎店对面的枪手向其猛烈开火。子弹九次击中汽车，但邹在这辆防弹车上的巨额投资经受住了考验，没有一颗子弹穿透装甲板。

邹、他的私人助理、一名保镖和一名司机均安然无恙。枪手也消失了，其中一人先将左轮手枪扔进了老介福的丝绸卷之间。

从刺客没有向车窗发射一枪这一事实可以推断，他们并非新手，因为他们理所当然地认为车窗也是防弹的。事实确实如此，车窗玻璃厚度超过一英寸。

袭击计划周密

这次暗杀肯定提前数日进行了周密计划，以确保万无一失，因为邹对其位于九江路230号大陆银行大楼的办公室的访问既稀少又不规律。唯有装甲板救了他的命，因为所有子弹都准确地瞄准了后座。

邹周一去办公室纯属偶然。那天下午，他在家中接到一个私人电话打来的呼叫，这部电话只有他使用，很少有人知道，电话告知他办公室里发生了40,000元的挪用公款案。他被要求前去处理。

据悉，他在下午3点后不久抵达那里。大约在5点钟，他再次离开，前往位于南阳路39号的家中。

邹通常走迂回路线。他的司机接到指令，绝不为交通信号灯停车，但如果红灯阻碍前行，则应左转。

被红灯困住

碰巧的是，当汽车从大陆银行大楼向外滩方向行驶时，在四川路路口被红灯拦住。

根据指令，司机左转，打算在南京路右转，从而继续前往外滩。然而，在南京路又遇到了一个红灯，他再次被迫左转。

因此，纯属偶然地，汽车行驶在南京路上，向西行进。然而，当它接近仅两个街区之外的河南路交叉口时，遭到了射击。

人们相信枪手不止两人，刺客部署在从大陆银行大楼引出的所有道路上，并且安排了望哨向枪手通报汽车的行驶方向。

在周一的枪击事件后，上海公共租界警务处逮捕了12名嫌疑人。当天大多数人被释放，但警方仍在对其余人员进行调查。

（批注：Lil 8 19/10）

值得注意的是，虽然十发子弹中有八发直接对准后座并直接命中，但没有一发进入车内。所有子弹都穿透了外部车身，但没有一发穿透装甲板，即汽车的内衬。

在该职位上一直待到1936年，随后在国民政府领导下，晋升为福建省烟酒税务局局长，该职位他一直担任至1937年7月，据他自己称，他于此时辞职。他接着解释说，1937年11月，在日本军方的同意和协助下，他开始重组安徽、浙江和江苏各省的统税局，由于取得成功，他被任命为该机构的总监，其主要办公地点位于九江路230号。他解释说，他很少去该办公室，尤其是最近，因为在过去五个月里，他收到了许多“恐吓信”，其中几封据称已交给中央巡捕房的小林（Kobayashi）副督察。他继续说，这些信件包含对他生命的威胁，并在某些情况下索要各种金额的款项，因此他极少离家外出。事实上，只有在极其必要的情况下，他才会前往九江路230号的办公室，大多数重要文件都送到家中供其签署等。在确实需要前往办公室的情况下，他解释说他会极度
